question: What the flameless n-heptane evaporation test in a controlled-atmosphere cone calorimeter allows to contrast about liquid heating and emission, without taking imposed irradiation for net absorbed heat.

source.citation: T. Beji, O. Helson, T. Rogaume, J. Luche, Experimental and numerical study on the evaporation rates of liquid fuels using a controlled atmosphere cone calorimeter, Fire Safety Journal 121 (2021) 103317
source.bibliographic_check: volume 121, article 103317 and year 2021 agree in Crossref and in the Ghent University record
source.reviewed_version: accepted version, 37 pages, distributed by the Ghent University repository
source.rights: Ghent record: no license, in copyright; Crossref: copyright 2021 Elsevier Ltd, all rights reserved
source.reason_not_archived: access to the accepted version is open, redistribution is not licensed
source.published_version_note: restricted in the Ghent record and closed at the publisher; not obtained
source.review: text of the 37 pages; set-up drawings and photographs (figures 1 and 2), tables 1 to 6 and figures 4, 6 and 7 read on page images

public_data.status: not located; whether they exist outside the laboratory is unknown
searched: accepted version: no data availability statement and no supplementary material mentioned
Crossref record of the article: no relation to a dataset or supplement
Ghent University record: two files, accepted version (open) and published article (restricted); no dataset
HAL record hal-03678931: metadata pointing to the Ghent file; no dataset
DataCite search for controlled atmosphere cone calorimeter evaporation: no record
Zenodo search for cone calorimeter heptane evaporation: no matching record
OpenAlex: no dataset attached to the work; seven citing works, none a data publication
MaCFP repositories macfp-db, matl-db and radi-db: no cone evaporation case

objects.nominal_irradiation: set point of the cone, checked with a heat flux gauge at one point before each test; nominal
objects.incident_irradiation: irradiation arriving at the regressing liquid surface during the test; calculated from geometry, not measured
objects.net_absorbed_heat: net heat crossing the boundary of the liquid; not identified
objects.demand_diagnostic: energy the evaporated mass and the warming liquid must have received; rebuilt from the observables, never an independent input

distance_initial_surface_to_cone_mm.where: protocol, step 1: 25 mm plus the lip

inner_side_mm.note: the drawing of figure 2 prints 95; the evaporation time of 168 s quoted for equation 14 is reproduced only with 0.10 m by 0.10 m

insulation.value: calcium silicate, about 18 mm at the sides and about 57 mm below

initial_mass_per_run.note: not reported; spillage before the test is reported for unnamed runs

initial_level_mm.where: pan depth minus lip; 250 ml over 98 mm by 98 mm gives 26.0

initial_temperature_c.where: section 2.2, stated range for all tests

upper_height_mm.where: section 2.2 and caption of figure 6 say 19; section 2.5.2 and captions of figures 14 and 15 say 20

in_liquid.value: two at the centre, two at 1 cm from the side, same heights

in_gas.value: two at about 33 mm from the bottom, centre and near the wall

published.value: centre pair only; the near-wall pair is said to be quite similar and is not shown; the gas pair is not shown

published_form.value: rate per unit area averaged every 15 s, as curves in figure 4

drift.note: a cooled gypsum board is fitted to limit it; no figure is given

check_before_each_test.value: Schmidt-Boelter gauge at the centre of the initial liquid surface position

oxygen.value: average not above 5 % in any test; typically below 2 % once stable
oxygen.note: series not published; the enclosure is not fully sealed

liquid_declared.where: table 1, taken by the authors from another paper
liquid_declared.note: used here only to reproduce the authors' own figures and to convert mass into a nominal level; the energy sums use the approved SimuFire profiles

reflectivity_assumed.where: section 3.3.3, taken from another paper for a wide range of liquids

authors_view_factor.note: average over the surface, the centre at the start taken as 1; the rim is not considered

flags: residual evaporation after the fall, attributed by the authors to spillage inside the enclosure
variant: holder not insulated, a vermiculite plate under the pan
residual evaporation after the fall, attributed by the authors to spillage inside the enclosure
residual evaporation after the fall visible in the figure; not named by the authors

test_matrix_notes.repetitions: three at each level in the reference configuration for n-heptane; two for methanol
test_matrix_notes.synchrony: the paper does not state that the mass and temperature curves labelled alike were acquired in the same run, though the protocol starts all acquisitions together; curves are paired here by label only
test_matrix_notes.low_oxygen: a means to prevent ignition; it is not a validation of under-ventilated residential combustion

criteria_fixed_before_reading_values: n-heptane only, the fuel with approved property profiles
reference configuration only: extraction on and insulated holder
every repetition that meets the two previous criteria at both irradiation levels, with no choice by agreement
a run enters the heating corpus only if both of its centre temperature curves are shown

digitisation.nature: digitisation of published figures; not raw data
digitisation.method: each marker located by matching its shape at multiples of 15 s; pixels of other curves treated as unknown
digitisation.reading_half_width: 1.5 pixels of the embedded bitmap, 3 pixels when partly hidden; a hidden marker is given as the range it can occupy
digitisation.reason_series_not_published: derived from figures of a copyrighted article; publication of the series is left to a decision of the project owner

support.rule: nothing is evaluated outside the approved supports and no reading is clipped to them

windows.first: from the first marker to the last marker at which the upper thermocouple, with its reading range, stays inside the liquid support: both centre thermocouples are liquid temperatures with support
windows.second: from the end of the first window to the last marker at which the lower thermocouple stays inside the support: only the lower thermocouple has support
windows.third: from the end of the second window to the end of the fall of the mass loss rate: no liquid temperature with support, mass only
windows.fixed_by: the property support and the readings themselves; no candidate model is involved

balance.control_volume: the liquid in the pan, open at its surface, at constant pressure
balance.sign: heat entering the liquid is positive
balance.identity: net heat = change of the sensible energy stored in the remaining liquid + mass emitted times the enthalpy from liquid at its initial state to vapour at the surface temperature
balance.feed_temperature_note: stated initial range 15 to 19 C; the upper thermocouple reads 20 to 30 C at the first marker, so the liquid is not uniform at the start; the range is an assumption interval, the liquid above the upper thermocouple is not measured
balance.surface_temperature_note: not measured; from the lowest temperature of the approved gas profile to the boiling point printed in the paper; mass emitted with a colder surface is not covered
not_in_the_control_volume: gas and vapour above the surface

frontier_terms.evidence: the check before each test is described; its reading and uncertainty are not reported
geometric factor under a uniform diffuse emitter; depends on a level that is not measured
shading calculated here with an opaque non-reflecting rim; reflection by the steel wall unknown
proposed by the authors; vapour concentration not measured
0.08 taken by the authors from another paper

gas thermocouples not published; set to zero in the authors' simulations

causes.status: proposed by the authors as likely; no vapour concentration was measured

causes.cause: further reduction of the view factor by the rim
causes.status: mentioned by the authors; not calculated by them

causes.cause: attenuation of the cone radiation by the vapour
causes.status: proposed by the authors; not measured

causes.cause: nominal irradiation lowered by 20 % in the simulations

authors_guide_lines.what: one vertical line per temperature panel: the authors' estimate of when the surface reaches the thermocouple, deduced from liquid heights calculated from the mass loss rate

independent_inputs: declared geometry of cone and pan
not_inputs: irradiation on the surface during the test
contract.initial_state: liquid between 15 and 19 C as stated, not uniform at the first marker; level known only as nominal
contrast_observables: accumulated mass per unit area at the markers
centre temperature at the lower height inside the first and second windows
centre temperature at the upper height inside the first window
boundary_conditions_unknown: gas temperature and vapour concentration above the liquid

uncertainties_known: spread between repetitions visible in the figures
calibratable_parameters: absorbed fraction of the nominal irradiation

cannot_be_claimed: net heat absorbed by the fuel
a mean or surface temperature of the liquid
